items.title: Humboldt Broncos families will appeal decision to dismiss lawsuit, lawyer says
items.description: A Saskatoon King's Bench Court judge dismissed the lawsuit initially filed in July 2018, just months after a semi-trailer went through a stop sign and collided with the junior hockey team’s bus, killing 16 people. Their lawyer says they will appeal.

items.title: N.S. fiddler Ashley MacIssac says AI content may have defamed him
items.description: Nova Scotia fiddler Ashley MacIsaac said the summary falsely asserted he had been convicted of a series of offences, including sexual assault and internet luring.

items.title: American billionaire wins defamation lawsuit against Peter Nygard
items.description: Billionaire hedge fund manager Louis Bacon has won his long-running defamation lawsuit alleging that former fashion mogul and convicted sex offender Peter Nygard spread lies about him during a public spat over their adjacent properties in the Bahamas.

items.title: Vancouver's newest transition house will help more women fleeing domestic violence
items.description: A 2023 B.C. Census report found that during a 24-hour period, 1,750 women, children and youth were helped through transition housing programs.

items.title: Sask. shoppers spending with intention this holiday season, report says
items.description: As shoppers in Saskatchewan head to shopping centres for last minute purchases, a new report suggests they are more likely to be spending with intention this year.

items.title: Here’s Why Involuntary Care Won’t Work for Most People
items.description: We need a total rethink of our failed approach to drugs and homelessness.

items.title: Manitoba Government Announces Second Round of Funding for Gate Project
Manitoba Government Invests $2.6 Million in Parkland and Westman Municipalities
The Calgary communities seeing effects of citywide rezoning the most and least
items.description: After Calgary city council voted to kickstart the process, a public hearing on whether or not to repeal citywide rezoning is expected in the spring.

items.title: FBI sought interview with former prince Andrew during Peter Nygard investigation
items.description: The FBI and U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York sought an interview with ex-prince Andrew for connections to Canadian sex offender and fashion mogul Peter Nygard.

items.title: Quebec Liberals to choose new leader at March 14 convention
items.description: The party announced Tuesday its nine-week leadership race will officially begin on Jan. 12.

items.title: Calgary Transit takes 19 shuttle buses out of service following fire
items.description: The shuttle buses were removed as part of an investigation into a Calgary Transit shuttle bus that caught fire on Nose Hill Drive N.W. earlier this month.

items.title: It's so cold in the Yukon, the power grid can't keep up
items.description: Frigid temperatures that hover around -40 C — or -50 C in some communities — continue to keep much of the territory in their grip. There’s no sign of that weather, patterns of which are coming from Siberia, easing up any time soon.

items.title: Bitter feud ensues after landlord's failed attempt to raise tenants' rent 65%
items.description: A New Brunswick tenant and his landlord have been in a bitter year-long dispute that involves a 65 per cent rent increase, a failed eviction attempt, and claims that the rental unit, a bungalow, is needed to house the owner's aging mother-in-law.
